description.narrative:
Oxfam in Cambodia through the Mekong Australia Partnership Phase 2 (MAP2), provided technical, financial, and accompaniment supports to civil society organizations, advocating for inclusive and effective water and climate-related policies at multiple levels. The project aligns with MAP2 goals: increasing leadership and economic opportunities for marginalized groups, promoting coordinated and sustainable water resource management, and reducing vulnerability to climate change. Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) through inclusive women’s leadership is a key program outcome, contributing to improved water resource governance and climate resilience.
The project overall goal is to contribute to Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Development of the Mekong basin in Cambodia by enhancing water resources governance and community resilience to climate and human induced changes in access to riverine natural resources.
1.4.1 Objectives (End of Program Outcome) 1. Targeted women leaders and representatives of marginalised groups supported by the Project in Cambodia, engage with and influence water governance and related disaster/climate change policies, events, platforms and processes at local, national and regional levels. 2. Targeted government line-ministries and intergovernmental organizations and non-state actors in Cambodia planning and decision-making processes in water governance and climate resilience include diverse groups and have policies/plans that reflect the perspectives of diverse actors supported by the Project. 3. Targeted riverine communities undertake inclusive analysis of local riverine water security including vulnerability to disaster risk and climate change and implement follow up adaptation plans.
1.4.2 Results (Intermediate outcomes) Intermediate Outcome 1: 1.1 More women anddiverse community leaders, including marginalised social groups actively engaging in WRG and climate related public events, platforms and fora at local, national and regional levels. 1.2 Target stakeholders at local, national and regional levels using GEDSI analysis within their policies and programs. 1.3 Increased public and community support for women and marginalised social groups to play leadership roles in targeted climate resilience and water resource policies and practices at all levels 1.4 Increased leadership capabilities and opportunity for women and diverse community members (including marginalised social groups) supported by the Project.
Intermediate Outcome 2: 2.1 Increased awareness of the impact of large-scale river infrastructure, Srepok 3A, Funan Techo Canal etc., resource use and disasters/climate change among the general public and water resource policy/decision makers. 2.2 Representatives of Project supported CSOs, CSO networks and communities including women leaders participating in WRG dialogue events and platforms with policy makers. 2.3 Targeted CSOs, CSO networks and community leaders with increased ability to represent the interests/demands of riverine communities.
Intermediate Outcome 3: 3.1 Targeted riverine communities have increased knowledge and awareness of local water security, climate and disaster risks mitigation and adaptation strategies 3.2 Targeted riverine community water resource and disaster risk management structures more inclusive of diverse community members (women, People with disability, Indigenous People andother marginalized social groups). 3.3 Targeted riverine households adopting disaster/climate resilient adaptive practices and/or behaviours. 1.5 How you want to achieve this: intervention strategy
The project will be implemented in partnership and collaborationwith CSOs, community network, private sector and government agencies including: Community level: theWomen's Leadership Fisheries Network in Cambodia (WLFN) and planned to strengthen a network of People with Disability (PWD) to amplify the voices of PWDs for inclusive development. National CSOs: the NGO Forum on Cambodia-Rive Coalition Cambodia (RCC), Culture and Environment Preservation Association (CEPA), My Village (MVi), 3S Rivers Protection Network (3SPN), People’s Actions for Inclusive Development (PAfID), Women withDisabilities Leadership and Advocacy Network (WWD-LAN). All of them are project partners who will work to empower with target communities and they are all part of the RCC network who will coordinate to bring the issues from riverine communities to influence watergovernance and climate resilience related policies at the national level.
Private sector actors include national/multilateral banks and companies engaged in water-related projects including those undertaking impact assessments and analyses or involved in the construction and/or operation of water infrastructure including the Ministry Water Resources and Meteorology (MOWRM) and Ministry of Environment (MoE), the National Committee for Disaster Management (NCDM) and inter-ministerial bodies such as the Tonle Sap Basin Authority, Cambodia National Mekong Committee (CNMC). Inall locations local government at the commune and district levels are key stakeholders for community-based activities. These agencies are the strategic partners for engagement and influencing for inclusive water resource governance and climate resilience.
In addition, this Program will complement other programs implemented by Oxfam in Cambodia especially the Natural Resource Governance (NRG) Programme Strategy. Water governance, climate resilience and GEDISI are the key focus of the programme. IP3 project together with other projects including the IrishAID funded Climate Change Resilience for All (CREFA) in Northwestern Cambodia, the European Union supported actions - Fisherfolk and the CircularEconomy in the Western Tonle Sap Lake, will complement each other to achieve the NRG programme aim to empower the natural resource dependent communities to better influence the governance of natural resources and build their resilience livelihoods. The project will maintain engagement with the Tonle Sap Water Security and Resilience program lead by Tonle Sap Authority in Cambodia. The lesson learned and practices from these programs will be used to inform the IP3 implementation to address long term adaptive capacity to strengthen long term community resiliencetoclimate change while gender justice at the core of Oxfam’s intervention.
Sustainable Outcomes: The program enhances the ability of community members, especially women leaders and CSO partners, toengage in WRG policy dialogue and improves the capacity of government and private sector actors for inclusive planning and consultation. Strengthening the capacity of riverine communities and CSOs ensures sustained relationships and skills post-program.Women's leadership development leads to better household and community management, improved livelihoods, and access to services, creating a ripple effect that inspires others and challenges norms that marginalize women.
1.5.2 Activities
Pillar 1: Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) andFeminist Influencing: focus is on advancing the leadership, agency and representation of diverse women leaders including Indigenous women, People with Disability and other marginalized social groups to influencing WRG and climate resilience policies and practices. Pillar One is a stand-aloneflagship pillar and is integrated into pillars two and three. Key activities include:
• Strengthen capacity and support women and representatives of marginalised groups to lead and represent in different eventsor platforms at all levels. • Strengthen agency of women/feminist leadership network in fisheries/WG and expansion. • Network women leaders with national and regional platform/conveneddialogues Eg.Huairou Commission’s women network (https://huairou.org/) •Organize leadership training or dialogues or Forum engaged women leaders and diverse groups on WG and climate related topics. • Develop/implement GEDSI Action Plans/Policies in Water Governance and Climate Resilience. • CSOs and community engage withgovernment and intergovernmental bodies to influence GEDSI in relevant policies (eg. GEDSI in Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0 and GEDSI in environment and climate change resilience, GEDSI in Disaster Risk Management etc.) • Develop GEDSI/PWD network to enforce GEDSI in WG and climate resilience. • Convene dialogues or workshop on GEDSI and Feminist Influencing engaging women and diverse community members (including marginalised social groups). These include IWD, World Water Day, IDAR, Woman and Water, World Fish Day etc.
Pillar 2: Water Resource Governance (WRG): focus on supporting civil society networks and coalitions to engage in WRG fora, policy development processes and mechanisms to ensure they are more inclusive of the needs and perspectives of civil society, diverse women and marginalized social groups (including youth, People withDisability and Indigenous Peoples).
• Facilitate with government, intergovernmental bodies and non-state actors, to provide space for diverse civil society actors (including women and marginalised social groups) to provide inputs to relevant policies/monitor their implementation. (eg. Provide inputs to the general strategic environmentalimpact assessment guideline, Sand Mining Strategic Environmental Impact Assessment guideline etc.) • Engage with and participate in the dialogues and inputting to the new development of national water governance strategies of MOWRAM process and support local partners and RCC network to influence this national WG policy. • Strengthen CSO leaders, network/coalition leaders and representative of marginalized groups to participate and influence relevant policies related to WRG and NR governance at all levels. • Develop narrative and provide policy inputs/commentsto targeted government, intergovernmental bodies and non-state actors to improve WRG policies/plans. • Conduct research or community led research WRG and climate resilience issues. • Apply FPAR for evidence-based documentation of river’s ecosystem changes • Engage with Media for visibility/influencing eg. Press release etc. • Organize a workshop or seminar engaging CSOs, community and government on sharing research findings, analysis, and keypublic communication pieces in an engaging and accessible way. • Convene inclusive dialogues or support CSOs and communities, especially women leaders to present key findings from FPAR or research in WRG dialogue events • Use outcome harvesting tools or other tracking tool to document the change (policy or practice)in targeted WRG processes such as sharing of information, statements of intent, notice periods, management of events, language, collection of disaggregated data etc) • Organize capacity buildingworkshop on advocacy, networking and policy engagement.
Pillar 3: Climate Resilient Communities focuses on enhancingcommunity resilience to human and climate-induced changes in river resource access within selected Mekong Sub-region communities.This is achieved through integrated community management of waterresources, including climate-resilient livelihoods, disaster/climate risk management, and sustainable watershed and fisheries management. The three pillars complement each other and address key transboundary water resource governance issues, such asriverdiversions, hydropower infrastructure, and changing flow regimes that threaten the livelihoods of diverse riverine communities.
• Conduct vulnerability risk assessment to define theclimate risk/impacts/needs ofclimate change affected communities. • SupportVDMG and CCDM to develop inclusive contingency plan/disaster risk management plan andimplementation • Target women, IPs and PWDs for Economic Empowerment eg. Climate Smart Livelihoods. •Engage with private sector to design nature/technology-based solutions to strengthen community's livelihood resilient to disaster and climate risks (e.g. climate smart agriculture, climate resilient irrigation etc.) • Formulate farmer producer group andmarket linkage - collaborate with other likeminded NGOs andtechnical consultants. • Support VDMG and CCDM to implement community-based early warning systems and increase subscribing to 1294 WES. • Organize joint awareness campaign or workshopto disseminate water resource/climate/disaster vulnerability analyses, and related follow-up strategies, among community members (including women and marginalized social groups) in targeted communities. Those include local water security, climate anddisaster risksmitigation and adaptation strategies. • Continue establish/strengthening CfiMCs and VDMGs by involving women, People with disability, Indigenous People and other marginalized social groups in Cfi and disaster risk management plan and implementation. •Strengthen functional relationship of national and sub-national authoritieswith Cfis and VDMGs and joint actions to address the issues of water resource/fisheries management and climate resilience. • Assesslocal ecosystem needs for disaster risk management and climate resilience.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
